problem: countColumn and findColumn give inconsistent columns for a tab followed by an Extend code point or a ZWJ
found: mirrors/cm6/state/src/column.ts:8-10 (countColumn) steps over a tab with i++ and then counts the next code point as a cluster of its own, while mirrors/cm6/state/src/column.ts:28-29 (findColumn) steps from the tab with findClusterBreak, which absorbs a following Extend code point or ZWJ (mirrors/marijn/find-cluster-break/src/index.js:53).

Fixtures: countColumn("\t\u0301x", 4) is 6 and countColumn("\t\u0301x", 4, 2) is 5 (F0482, F0483); findColumn("\t\u0301x", 4, 4) is 2 and findColumn("\t\u0301x", 5, 4) is 3 (F0486, F0485), so findColumn(s, countColumn(s, 4, 2), 4) is 3, not 2.
open_because: The code of both functions is explicit, and neither their doc comments (column.ts:3-4, :19-23) nor any test in mirrors/cm6/state/test (grep: neither function is tested there) says whether the two are meant to be inverse; no decision in force covers it.
bears_on: view rectangular-selection.ts:48 computes a column with countColumn and rectangular-selection.ts:26-30 maps columns back with findColumn, so a rectangle over a line starting with a tab followed by a combining mark selects at an offset one column off from the one clicked (deduction from the code; not run in a view).

In gen-column.ts (seed 20261111), findColumn(s, countColumn(s, tabSize, i), tabSize) == i fails at some cluster boundary i for 20 of 150 random strings (field roundTrip of F3000-F3149); every failing string contains a tab followed by an Extend code point or a ZWJ, and none of the 130 others does. A tab after a ZWJ is handled the same way by both functions (countColumn B8, findColumn B9).
A tab followed by a combining mark or ZWJ is rare in source text (deduction).
Reproducing cm6 exactly requires stepping tabs differently in the two functions; a shared cluster walker would change one of them.
blocks: The implementation of countColumn and findColumn (state.cm6.216, state.cm6.217), from S5; no other S2 work.

problem: A partial text cursor (Text.iterRange) given a skip can return text outside its range or skip the wrong distance
found: mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:507-511 (PartialTextCursor.next) clips a positive skip with Math.min(skip, this.to - this.pos) and a negative one with Math.max(skip, this.from - this.pos), the forward bounds, whatever the cursor direction; pos starts at 0 for a forward cursor and at text.length for a reverse one (:485).

Reverse cursor, first call: Text.of(["one", "two", "", "three", "four"]).iterRange(12, 2).next(2).value is "four" (positions 15-19, outside [2, 12)) (F0870); Text.of(["abcdefgh"]).iterRange(6, 2).next(1).value is "cdefgh" (positions 2-8) (F0872); iterRange(8, 2).next(1) returns "cdefgh", the skip ignored (F0873).
Forward cursor, first call with a negative skip: iterRange(2, 12).next(-5).value is "two" (position 4) where the next() without skip gives "e" at 2 (F0869).
After the first step the forward cursor behaves as a clipped raw cursor (F0868, gen-text.ts checks skips in -3..3 after the first step on forward ranges).
open_because: The interface documents next(skip) as skipping positions after the current position (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:16-19) and iterRange as running in reverse when from > to (:106-108), which the code does not do in these cases; no cm6 test passes a skip to an iterRange cursor (mirrors/cm6/state/test/test-text.ts:151-168 call next() only), and no decision in force covers it.
bears_on: No cm6 consumer passes a skip to an iterRange cursor: search cursor.ts:52, merge deco.ts:55, view matchdecorator.ts:8 and language matchbrackets.ts:197 call next() without arguments (grep of mirrors/cm6/*/src); skips are passed only to raw cursors from Text.iter (language.ts:267, isolate.ts:107, lint.ts:138, regexp.ts:50, buildtile.ts:267).
Third-party code calling iterRange(...).next(skip) observes the values recorded in F0869-F0873; reproducing them requires the same clipping formula (deduction).
The forward cursor without skip, the reverse cursor without skip and the raw cursors with any skip match the position model checked on 300 seeded cases (gen-text.ts).
blocks: The behaviors and port of PartialTextCursor.next with a skip (state.cm6.225 B7, B8), from S5.

problem: The cm6 test "returns the correct strings for slice" overwrites its random range and checks one fixed slice 400 times
found: mirrors/cm6/state/test/test-text.ts:93-98: each of 400 iterations draws start and end with Math.random() (:94-95) and then sets start = 4150; end = 4160 (:96) before asserting doc.slice(start, end).toString() == str.slice(start, end) (:97).
Both sides are "0830\n0831\n" on every iteration (F5005); the random values are never used, including the i == 0 and i == 399 special cases at :94-95 that aim at the document start and end.
Test row test-text#13 records the test as it is.
open_because: The code is unambiguous about what runs; whether the test is meant to cover random ranges (as the loop and the special cases at :94-95 suggest) cannot be read from the code, and the specification method records such a test as found and never corrects it (docs/workflow/specification.md §6).
bears_on: A port that reproduces the test exactly covers one slice inside a single leaf; random slices of the same document are covered elsewhere by test-text#28 (sliceString and slice on doc0 at 500 random ranges) and by gen-text.ts (seeded slices checked against a string model).

The slice 4150-4160 lies inside one leaf of a 1000-line node document, so Text.slice B3 (sharing whole children) is not exercised by this test (deduction from the shape: lines 830-831 sit in one 32-line leaf).
blocks: How test-text#13 is ported (test writing, S2 tests stage onward); no behavior waits on it.
